summary: Unexpected P99 latency variance traced to ephemeral training job sweep impacting dedicated pool throughput
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC Parkly Labs reported intermittent P99 latency spikes (3-7x baseline) and a 20-40% drop in sustained throughput on their dedicated capacity pool. The spikes are brief (30-90s) but frequent across a 6-hour window. Impact: customer-facing inference degraded for latency-sensitive endpoints; some user requests timed out and retried, increasing load. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 serving redwood-open-7b-v2 for Parkly Labs; autoscaler configured with aggressive downscale cooldown (2m) and default min_replicas=2.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Call Parkly Labs' reserved model route during the reported window (prod us-east). 2) Observe transient p99 latency spikes and drop in throughput in Console > Routes > Parkly-Prod > Metrics. 3) Correlate with node-level GPU attach/detach events in infra logs. Note: spikes are intermittent and harder to reproduce outside the customer's traffic pattern (short, high-frequency small-stream bursts).
logs:
- Metrics snapshot (03:12 UTC): p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 2.6s (baseline p99 ~350ms).
- Node events: repeated ephemeral eviction events on gpu-node-ue1-042 and gpu-node-ue1-047 at 03:05/03:08/03:11 UTC.
- Scheduler trace: preemptive allocation request from tenant id=tenant-ephemeral-981; priority tag 'batch-job' unset, landed on same rack as Parkly.
- Autoscaler logs: scale_down executed at 03:06 UTC (from 6->3 rep), then scale_up at 03:09 UTC (3->7) matching spikes.
- KV cache metrics: sudden cache misses rose 3x during spike windows.
comments: Ava Martinez (Support): Customer reports repeated user-facing timeouts; collected request IDs and windowed traces; escalated to SRE.
Devon Chen (SRE): Observed node-level evictions and autoscaler thrash. Initial hypothesis: co-located ephemeral training/batch jobs created IO / cuda contention causing inference batch serialization.
Priya Rao (Scheduler Eng): Found job submission from internal orchestration (tenant-ephemeral-981) that bypassed tenant-affinity constraints; PR opened to enforce affinity tagging (see related PR).
SRE on-call (Liam O'Connor): Temporarily bumped Parkly's min_replicas to 4 and set autoscaler downscale cooldown to 10m as a mitigation; customer reports reduced p99 spikes after mitigation.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 03:00–03:30 UTC repeated P99 spikes correlated with short-lived batch training jobs launched by tenant-ephemeral-981 that saturated GPU PCIe bandwidth and triggered CUDA context flushes on shared nodes. The scheduler allowed these jobs onto nodes with active inference slots due to a missing hard-affinity label on ephemeral tenant jobs. Autoscaler misinterpreted the load pattern: short bursts caused rapid scale-down (cooldown too short) then aggressive scale-up when requests queued, producing oscillation and increasing tail latency. Evidence: node GPU utilization logs show IO saturation concurrent with high packet drops on RDMA, and the GPU process list shows large ephemeral processes (data loader workers). Investigation links: Slack #support thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/support/p/CL7J9J2), infra dashboard panels (infra.redwood.ai/d/peaky-gpu), and scheduler trace (trace_id: b3f0a8a2).
root_cause_hypothesis: A combination of: 1) ephemeral batch/training jobs scheduled onto shared nodes (no hard tenant affinity), causing noisy-neighbor PCIe/RDMA contention and intermittent CUDA context evictions; 2) autoscaler downscale cooldown set too short, leading to reactive oscillation; 3) KV cache churn from evicted contexts increasing per-request compute and amplifying latency.
resolution: Short-term mitigations applied 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC: - Bumped Parkly min_replicas to 4 and increased autoscaler downscale cooldown to 10m to avoid rapid oscillation. - Quarantined tenant-ephemeral-981 jobs by applying temporary hard-affinity (node isolation) and throttled their scheduling. Outcome: P99 spikes reduced to ~1.3x baseline; throughput stabilized. Long-term fixes in progress: - Scheduler patch to enforce tenant-affinity labels and prevent batch jobs landing on inference nodes (PR #4821). - Autoscaler tuning: increase default downscale cooldown and add short-burst detection to avoid scaling on sub-2m transients. - Add detection alert and automated temporary pinning when KV cache evictions exceed threshold. Rollout plan: Scheduler patch staged to canary cluster 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-18 after validation. Autoscaler tuning merged 2026-03-11, will be monitored for 48h.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem draft assigned to Devon Chen (target 2026-03-18). 2) Add a conservative default for min_replicas for latency-sensitive dedicated pools (prod policy update). 3) Implement a monitor in Console to flag short-burst oscillation patterns (pager rule). 4) Notify affected customers and provide remediation guidance for noisy tenant detection.
resolution_notes: Mitigation successful in reducing immediate customer impact. SRE and Scheduler teams collaborating on permanent fixes. Customer (Parkly Labs) acknowledged reduced errors and requested timeline for complete fix; provided ETA and will schedule a follow-up sync.
